items.item_text: Board Certified/Eligible in Radiology
An active/eligible California medical license
Fellowship training or demonstrated experience in musculoskeletal (MSK), body imaging, or chest/abdominal radiology

UCLA Health is seeking a board-certified/board-eligible Radiologist to join our growing team in a fully remote position. This role offers the opportunity to practice diagnostic radiology within a collaborative, high-volume environment, supported by the resources of a leading academic health system.

This position is designed for radiologists who enjoy a broad scope of practice, with flexibility to incorporate subspecialty interests such as musculoskeletal (MSK), body imaging, or chest/abdominal radiology. Physicians will work closely with multidisciplinary teams to deliver timely, high-quality imaging interpretation and support patient care across a diverse clinical population.

This is a clinically focused position with no required teaching or research responsibilities, offering physicians the opportunity to focus on clinical practice while remaining connected to the expertise and resources of an academic health system.
Learn more about the Department of Radiology, here: [http:]https://www.uclahealth.org/departments/radiologyhere.
Provide diagnostic radiology interpretation across a variety of imaging modalities
Interpret imaging studies including CT, MRI, ultrasound, and X-ray
Collaborate with referring providers and clinical teams to support accurate and timely diagnosis
Contribute to quality improvement and patient safety initiatives
Practice fully remotely while contributing to patient care across the UCLA Health system
Utilize your breadth of diagnostic expertise across a diverse and high-volume clinical population
Incorporate subspecialty interests within a broad diagnostic radiology practice
Collaborate with multidisciplinary clinical teams across one of the nation’s leading academic health systems
Work with advanced imaging technologies and an integrated Epic environment
Preferred Qualifications:
Interest in working within a collaborative, multidisciplinary care environment

the final candidate who accepts an offer of employment will be required to disclose if they have been subject to any final administrative or judicial decisions within the last seven years determining that they committed any misconduct; or have filed an appeal of a finding of substantiated misconduct with a previous employer.
Strong general radiology skillset across multiple modalities
